title: November Days Out: Quieter, Cheaper Family Adventures
description: November family days out: why it’s a quiet, cheaper month, plus fireworks, woodland walks, museums, early festive events and rainy-day backups.
h1: November days out: quieter, cheaper adventures
intro: November is the secret season. Summer crowds are gone, Christmas hasn’t hit yet, and many attractions are calmer. Here’s how to make the most of it.

image.alt: A child in yellow wellies walking through autumn leaves

cardText: Why November is quiet and cheap, and what to do with it.

blocks.title: Scout’s November tip
blocks.text: Check opening dates. Some outdoor attractions close for winter or open only at weekends from November, while indoor ones carry on as normal.

sections.html: Firework displays around Bonfire Night: see Bonfire Night with kids. Woodland walks are at their crunchiest, and wildlife like deer are easy to spot. See wildlife watching.

• Museums and science centres.
  • Indoor water parks.
  • Trampoline parks, bowling and climbing.
  • Board game cafés.
Christmas markets, light trails and ice rinks start to open. Book the big festive days now: see the advent calendar of days out.

faqs.q: Is November a good time for days out?
faqs.a: Yes. Attractions are often quieter and some offer off-peak prices. Check opening dates, as some outdoor attractions reduce hours in winter.
